data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The forbidden-case set must include a fixture-quotient mutation where the suite is bypassed by inflating the frozen lease fixture into a full manifest, which trivially satisfies binding constraints without invoking lease-mismatch detection; this defeats the false-green risk mitigation because any test harness that only asserts route validity via manifest lookups will pass silently when the lease-mismatch pre-check is skipped.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the firewall implementation guarantees that lease-mismatch pre-checks run before manifest resolution regardless of fixture type, this mutation would fail the suite rather than pass silently, invalidating the forbidden case.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the test harness includes a branch-coverage assertion that explicitly requires the lease-mismatch code path to be entered, the full-manifest mutation would be caught.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The frozen lease alone is intended to be a minimal, self-contained fixture: it carries a typed route identity and an endpoint identity hash, and the firewall must reject the request before any provider call if the endpoint identity in the lease disagrees with the frozen seat. However, if a mutation replaces the lease-only fixture with a full manifest that includes the drifted endpoint, the binding validation logic may consume the manifest directly and resolve the seat binding through a separate path that never executes the lease-mismatch code. This creates a false-green: the suite reports coverage success because the binding succeeds, but the specific typed lease-mismatch refusal (refusal 1) was never exercised. The mechanism is causal because the mutation alters the test fixture's structural type, which changes which validation branch is taken at runtime.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
